source: door-app/research/roof-damage-thresholds-2026-10.md (2026-10-05). Field-damage thresholds, not product ratings. Each company can change them under Storm list > Prices and thresholds.

notes.asphalt: Haag/Marshall 2002 field table: 3-tab 1.00 in, laminated 1.25 in (A). New shingles good to about 1.5 in (IBHS). By roof age: under 6 years 1.5, 6 to 10 years 1.25, over 10 years 1.0. Wind: NWS spotter guide, 58 to 74 mph removes shingles.
notes.tile: Concrete tile 1.75 in (Haag 2002, A); clay 1.5 to 1.75 (B only). IBHS: tile roofs can leak from 50 mph.
notes.shake: Wood shakes 1.50 in, wood shingles 1.25 in (Haag 2002, A). Wind 65 mph (EF-scale degree of damage 1, Texas Tech 2006).
notes.metal: No functional hail threshold from a primary source; 2 in is denting, not leaking (UL 2218 Class 4 is a test, not a threshold). Wind 74 mph (EF-scale metal panels).
notes.flat: Built-up with gravel 2.50 in (Haag 2002, A); single-ply 2 in (FM 4470 test, B). The lower figure is used. Wind 72 mph (EF-scale low-slope covering loss, lower bound).
notes.slate: 1.5 to 1.75 in from one B source; left blank rather than pick one. Set your own.

bands: Likely: the hail at the house is at or over the threshold. Possible: within a quarter inch under it. The quarter inch is this app's rule, not a sourced figure; radar hail (MESH) often reads under what people report.
